title: 2016 AMC 12B Problem 14
statement: The sum of an infinite geometric series is a positive number \(S,\) and the second term in the series is \(1.\) What is the smallest possible value of \(S?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(r\) be the common ratio. Since the second term is \(1,\) the first term is \(\dfrac1r,\) so \(S=\dfrac{\frac{1}{r}}{1-r}=\dfrac{1}{r-r^2}.\) Convergence requires \(|r|\lt1,\) and \(S\gt0\) then forces \(0\lt r\lt1.\) Therefore \(S\) is smallest when \(r-r^2\) is largest. The parabola \(r-r^2\) peaks at \(r=\tfrac12,\) where it equals \(\tfrac14,\) so the smallest value of \(S\) is \(\dfrac{1}{\frac{1}{4}}=4.\)

Thus, the correct answer is E.
